title: Think as You Like but Behave Like Others
coreMove: Protect independent thought by adapting outward behavior to the room's tolerance
sourcePressure: Chapter 38 centers on outward conformity as a way of protecting inner difference in environments that punish visible deviation. The law values surface adaptation because obvious nonconformity can trigger hostility, envy, or exclusion before independent thought has room to work. Its limit is that camouflage fails when it becomes permanent surrender, moral collapse, or loss of the independence it was meant to protect. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
